classification.difficultyReason: Construct a right-angled triangle from a bearing and identify the southward distance needed to reach the east–west line through the starting point.

content.prompt:
A tank moves 13.5 km from point $A$ on a bearing of $042^{\circ}$ to point $B$.
From point $B$, how far due south must the tank travel to be at a point due east of point $A$?
Give the answer correct to the nearest metre.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14, blank compass rose below the prompt
spec.description: Four black compass arrows and N, E, S, W labels, with an unlabelled centre. No journey, bearing or distance is supplied in the figure.
spec.mathematics: North is upward, east rightward, south downward and west leftward.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent blank drawing scaffold; all route and triangle annotations belong to the response.

answer.worked:
Let $C$ be the point due east of $A$ and due south of $B$. Then $\angle BAC=90^{\circ}-42^{\circ}=48^{\circ}$ and $BC=x$.
$$\begin{align*}
\sin48^{\circ}&=\frac{x}{13.5}\\
x&=13.5\sin48^{\circ}\\
x&\approx10.032\text{ km}
\end{align*}$$
The tank must travel $10\,032\text{ m}$ due south, to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Completed right-angled triangle with the initial northeast journey, clockwise bearing from north, acute reference angle and subsequent southward leg.
spec.mathematics: B is at offset (3 sin 42°, 3 cos 42°) from A in drawing units. C is vertically below B and due east of A. AB represents 13.5 km; BC is the required distance.
